results.title: SuperRelay vs Ferndesk — for software teams
results.content:
# SuperRelay vs Ferndesk

Ferndesk is a help center that checks every article against your codebase and product, catches what changed, and drafts the fixes. It is a docs product first, with AI answers and a widget on top and escalation to Intercom, Zendesk, or Help Scout for the conversations. SuperRelay is the whole support stack in one place, with a knowledge base you can sync from markdown but no verification against your code.

Start free   Ask about switching [...] Start free   Ask about switching

| At a glance | SuperRelay | Ferndesk |
 --- 
| Made for | Software and SaaS teams | Software teams whose docs go stale |
| Pricing model | By products and seats, free plan included | Per workspace, tiered |
| AI agent grounded in your knowledge base |  | Answers from verified docs |
| AI agent can act inside your product via your API |  | — |
| Written handoff briefing when AI escalates to a human |  | — |
| Live visitor presence and session view |  | — |
| Help center, changelog, and feature requests embeddable in your product |  | — |

## Which one is for you?

### Choose Ferndesk if… [...] ## Which one is for you?

### Choose Ferndesk if…

 Keeping docs accurate is your main problem and you want them checked against your codebase
 You're happy with your current support tool and only want to replace the help center
 You want the article drafted from the pull request before the release ships

### Choose SuperRelay if…

 You want the inbox, an AI agent, a help desk, and a knowledge base in one plan instead of four subscriptions
 You want an agent that answers from your docs and can act inside your product through your own API
 You want a written briefing when the agent hands off, so nobody has to read a transcript
 You want the docs, the widget, and the agent to run off one knowledge base without a second tool for conversations
